_comment: Both ports are fixed, and neither may be reassigned. `autoPort: true` looks harmless and
is not: on this project a moved port fails silently rather than loudly.
1. `BACKEND_PORT = 8080` is a hardcoded constant in frontend/src/lib/apiClient.ts:16.
`apiBase()` derives the host from wherever the page was opened but always appends
this port, so every API call goes to :8080 whatever the backend is listening on.
outright that it must match the Google console entry exactly, INCLUDING THE PORT.
A moved port cannot be fixed locally — it needs an edit in Google Cloud.
FRONTEND, port 3000 — CORS, and this one was `autoPort: true` until 2026-09-05:
The backend's ALLOWED_ORIGINS and FRONTEND_ORIGIN both name localhost:3000. A frontend
that started on 3001 would have every credentialed request rejected by the browser with
no server error, so the whole app would read as signed-out with nothing in any log.
Failing to start is strictly better than that.
If a port is genuinely occupied, free it rather than reassigning it.
